Density of the Product of Three Normal Variables

Source: R/dprodnormal3.R
dprodnormal3.Rd

Exact density of \(X_1 X_2 X_3\) when \((X_1, X_2, X_3)\) is trivariate normal with mean mean and covariance cov, the density counterpart of pprodnormal3(). No closed form is known for the general case (Gaunt, 2022), so the density is a two-dimensional integral: conditioning on \(X_1 = x\) makes \((X_2, X_3)\) bivariate normal, whose product has the density of dprodnormal(), and $$f(v) = \int \phi(x; \mu_1, \sigma_1^2)\, f_{X_2 X_3 \mid x}(v / x)\, / |x|\, dx.$$ The inner density is the Rohatgi/Glen integral used by dprodnormal() (conditional means and the partial correlation are computed per \(x\)).

Usage

dprodnormal3(x, mean, cov, log = FALSE)

Arguments

x

Numeric vector of quantiles.

mean

Numeric vector of means of length 3.

cov

3x3 covariance matrix; must be positive definite.

log

Logical; return the log density.

Value

Numeric vector of densities, the length of x.

Details

The density has a logarithmic singularity at exactly 0 (returned as Inf), as for dprodnormal(). Unlike pprodnormal3(), zero-variance components are not supported: a point mass has no density.

References

Gaunt, R. E. (2022). On the product of three normal random variables. See also the references of dprodnormal().

See also

pprodnormal3() for the CDF, dprodnormal() for two factors.

Examples

Sigma <- matrix(c(1, .3, .2, .3, 1, .1, .2, .1, 1), 3)
dprodnormal3(c(0.1, 0.5, 1), mean = c(0.5, 0.4, 0.3), cov = Sigma)
#> [1] 0.8662498 0.2349625 0.1075559
